posts.text:
Elon's donation illustrates why Trump Accounts are a fantastic new model for giving.

To date, Elon has given $8.3 billion to his foundation, though very little of that has reached operating charities. Most of the money remains in the foundation or has been transferred to his personal DAF or a nonprofit he controls. The benefit to society has been minimal.

He's been skeptical of traditional philanthropy, arguing "If you care about the reality of doing good and not the perception of doing good, then it is very hard to give away money effectively."

He's right that giving away billions of dollars effectively is difficult, especially if you have a day job, or three. I've seen many donors get frustrated by the process and then their giving doesn't match their philanthropic intent. 

That's what makes Trump accounts so powerful. The impact is direct. Every dollar goes to the intended beneficiaries. And the model is infinitely scalable.

With a single donation, Musk will deliver more direct philanthropic benefit than through all his previous giving combined. And he's promising to do it every year. It's easy. It's effective. It's universal, at least to American children.

Regardless of your view of Trump, regardless of your view of Elon, this form of giving is a great alternative model to traditional philanthropy and should be applauded.

🚨 HOLY CRAP! Somebody got inside the system the Air Force uses to track bombs and missiles at more than 200 bases.

According to Reuters, citing people familiar with the matter, hackers breached Cloud One, the Air Force's flagship cloud platform. It runs personnel, pay, logistics and maintenance apps. 

It also runs air defense radar feeds for North America and the munitions tracking system.

THEY FOUND IT DURING AN UPGRADE, NOT BECAUSE ANYBODY CAUGHT IT. 

This makes me sick. Back in 2023, Cloud One's leadership bragged about a "100% success rate" against hackers and said there was "no room for error." 

Now Reuters says nobody can tell us who got in, how much they saw, or whether they took anything. Cyber Command has been called in to clean it up.

Taxpayers spent years paying Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, Google and the big defense contractors to build this. 

When the system guarding our munitions gets cracked open, somebody has to get fired. Not reassigned… Fired! 

Our enemies are watching. Find out who did this and make them pay.

18-year-old Elias Matanios Mardini, a young Syrian Christian from the village of Maarouneh, was found shot dead on the road connecting his hometown with Saydnaya in the Damascus countryside.

His body bore multiple gunshot wounds. He was killed alongside another young Christian, 17-year-old Élie Asaad Hilaleh.

Since December 2024, Christian communities have faced escalating violence, kidnappings, intimidation, and religious discrimination.

Just days before Elias’s death, armed men stormed the Cathedral of Our Lady of Peace in Homs, assaulting Archbishop Youhanna Abdo Arbash and stealing religious valuables, including his golden cross.

The patriarchs of Syria’s three largest Christian churches have condemned the recurring attacks and the government's failure to protect their communities.

Rest in peace, Elias. ✝️
